title: Maritime trade routes are under threat—and markets still underprice the risks
gist: The author argues the world's key waterways—Hormuz, Bab al-Mandab, the Black Sea, European rivers, and the Panama Canal—are under simultaneous geopolitical and climate pressure, and that markets have not yet priced the resulting rise in shipping costs, inflation, and food and fertilizer shortages. The piece forecasts higher costs over three months, deepening shortages and inflation in the medium term, and potential permanent reshaping of global trade routes.

insights.claim: The Strait of Hormuz is effectively blocked, and maritime trade through it accounts for 19 percent of global LNG, 25 percent of global oil trade, and 30 percent of fertilizer trade, already pushing up prices for all three commodities.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Quantifies the single largest disruption and its direct exposure to energy and fertilizer prices, a core inflation vector.
insights.quote: Maritime trade through the strait accounts for 19 percent of global liquefied natural gas (LNG), 25 percent of global oil trade, and 30 percent of fertilizer trade.
insights.locator: In terms of sheer trade volume

insights.claim: The resumption of Houthi attacks on vessels has effectively created an informal blockade at the Bab al-Mandab Strait, through which more than 10 percent of global trade passes, including significant global petroleum products via Red Sea ports.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: A second Middle East chokepoint under blockade compounds rerouting costs around Africa.
insights.locator: But the situation at the Bab al-Mandab

insights.claim: European drought has pushed the Rhine to the lowest water levels ever recorded and the Danube to a thirty-year low, disrupting major arteries of European trade including a key Rhine route for oil and LNG.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Climate-driven low water adds an inland-transport shock on top of maritime disruption, raising European energy logistics costs.
insights.quote: The Rhine has reached the lowest water levels ever recorded, and the Danube has fallen to a thirty-year low

insights.claim: Black Sea routes transport petroleum, fertilizer, and up to a quarter of global wheat supplies, and Russia's continued aggression is making commercial shipping there increasingly hazardous with numerous vessels attacked.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Wheat exposure ties the Black Sea disruption directly to global food security and grain prices.

insights.claim: About 6 percent of global trade passes through the Panama Canal, with over 70 percent of transiting vessels bound for or departing a US port, and falling Gatun Lake levels plus a strong El Niño have forced the Canal Authority to restrict vessel drafts with further limits in late August and early September.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Draft restrictions concentrate the hit on US-bound trade just before the holiday shipping season.
insights.locator: On the other side of the world

insights.claim: Maritime transport accounts for more than 80 percent of the world's goods, so rising shipping costs from rerouting and higher insurance premiums will inevitably filter through to consumers.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Establishes the transmission channel from chokepoint disruption to broad consumer inflation.
insights.quote: The resulting rise in maritime transport costs, which accounts for more than 80 percent of the world’s goods, will inevitably filter through to consumers.

insights.claim: Rerouting around Africa can add up to two weeks to a voyage while increasing fuel and labor costs, and for EU-serving ships longer routes raise emissions and shipping costs under the EU emissions trading system.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: The EU ETS adds a regulatory cost multiplier to rerouting, a specific margin risk for Europe-facing carriers.

insights.claim: The author argues price increases will be sticky even if routes reopen, because berths will be full, suppliers will have booked alternatives, and insurers will keep rates high while assessing renewed hostility and climate risk.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Stickiness means the inflation impulse outlasts the disruption itself, relevant to rate-path expectations.
insights.quote: even if routes reopen, these price increases are likely to be sticky.

insights.claim: Any Middle East truce will still require a lengthy demining process that could take months, during which vessel passage remains restricted to select secured routes.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Even a diplomatic breakthrough would not quickly restore shipping capacity, extending the disruption timeline.
insights.locator: Any potential truce in the Middle East

insights.claim: Northern Hemisphere farmers faced a fertilizer price surge this spring that could spread to the Southern Hemisphere if Middle East routes stay blocked, reducing crop yields and driving up food prices and food insecurity.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Direct pathway from shipping disruption to a global fertilizer-to-food-price cascade.
insights.locator: This spring, farmers in the Northern Hemisphere

insights.claim: Late-summer cargo shipments carry holiday goods from Asia for Christmas, so Panama Canal draft restrictions and delays could leave retailers facing higher prices and tighter delivery windows.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Flags a concrete seasonal retail and consumer-goods inflation risk for Q4.

insights.claim: Access to scarce essential supplies will increasingly favor those with money or domestic resources, as reserves provide only a temporary buffer and alternative sources are difficult to secure.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Implies widening resource inequality between resource-rich and import-dependent nations under sustained disruption.

insights.claim: The author argues insurers will increasingly price war and climate risks into coverage, making the most exposed trade routes more expensive to operate and ultimately determining which routes remain commercially viable.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Insurance repricing could permanently redraw the map of viable trade routes, a durable structural shift.

insights.claim: Sustained high energy costs will raise production costs for steel, chemicals, cement, and paper, potentially shifting demand toward domestic suppliers who are themselves exposed to higher energy costs, forcing firms to pass costs on or cut operations and employment.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Links maritime disruption to energy-intensive industrial margins and employment, broadening the macro impact.

insights.claim: The author's central thesis is that markets have yet to fully price in maritime trade risks, while policymakers should not make the same mistake because maritime routes often provide the first warning signs of broader disruption.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Explicit claim of market mispricing is the core actionable signal for positioning in shipping, commodities, and inflation hedges.
insights.quote: While markets have yet to fully price in these risks, policymakers should not make the same mistake.
